simple.meaning: מַחְלֻי (machluy) is a Hebrew word meaning “a disease.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: מַחְלֻי (H4251) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 2 Chronicles 24:25, with occurrences in 2 Chronicles.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַחְלֻי (H4251) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in מַחְלֻי (H4251) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: מַחְלֻי (machluy) / H4251 is traced through 2 Chronicles 24:25 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H4251. machluy or machaluy [ מַהֲלוּי ] noun masculine sickness, suffering (caused by wounds, compare חלה 2Kin 8:29 ) — only plural intensive מַחֲלֻיִים 2Chr 24:25 .

occurrences.englishText: When they had departed from him (for they left him very sick), his own servants conspired against him for the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest, and killed him on his bed, and he died. They buried him in David’s city, but they didn’t bury him in the tombs of the kings.
